question: What is the main idea of this video?
answer: The video introduces the vector as the basic building block of linear algebra and makes sure everyone shares the same picture of what a vector is. It presents three related views. To a physics student, a vector is an arrow defined by its length and direction. To a computer science student, it is an ordered list of numbers. To a mathematician, it is anything that can be sensibly added together and multiplied by a number. It then highlights two core operations that run through all of linear algebra: vector addition and scalar multiplication, where a scalar is a number that stretches or shrinks a vector. The key takeaway is that the power of linear algebra comes less from picking one view and more from being able to translate back and forth between the geometric picture and the numerical one. That lets data analysts visualize lists of numbers, and lets physicists and graphics programmers describe space with numbers a computer can work with.

The usefulness of linear algebra has less to do with either one of these views than it does with the ability to translate back and forth between them. It gives the data analyst a nice way to conceptualize many lists of numbers in a visual way, which can seriously clarify patterns in data and give a global view of what certain operations do. And on the flip side, it gives people like physicists and computer graphics programmers a language to describe space and the manipulation of space using numbers that can be crunched and run through a computer.
